module_role: Source-synchronous low-power mobile memory device intended to be paired with an LPDDR5 memory controller + PHY. JESD209-5 standardizes the SDRAM component side (ballout, low-voltage signaling, the 7-bit DDR CA command/address protocol, WCK/RDQS clocking, mode registers, AC timing). The controller / PHY side is OUT of scope but must implement: (a) quarter-speed CK generation + on-demand full-speed WCK, (b) WCK2CK synchronization (WS_FS/WS_RD/WS_WR), (c) a command scheduler honouring tRCD/tRP/tRAS/tRC/tRRD_L/tRRD_S/tFAW/tCCD_L/tCCD_S/tWR/tWTR/tRFCab/tRFCpb/tREFI, (d) ZQ calibration, (e) DQ/RDQS read training and WCK write training with DFE/equalization, (f) link-ECC encode/decode and DBI, (g) DVFS / frequency-set-point management, (h) per-bank state tracking. Concrete LPDDR5 controller IP appears in mobile SoCs (Snapdragon, Apple M-series, MediaTek Dimensity, Kirin) and IP vendors (Synopsys, Cadence).

integration_overview.channel_organization: Typically two x16 channels per package; each channel has its own CK / WCK / RDQS / CA / CS / DQ / DMI; internal two-deck organization for finer power/access granularity.
integration_overview.wire_directions: CK, WCK, CA[6:0], CS, RESET_n: controller → DRAM. RDQS: DRAM → controller (read). DQ, DMI: bidirectional. ZQ: external reference resistor. VDD1/VDD2H/VDD2L/VDDQ + grounds: supplies.
integration_overview.no_cke: There is NO Clock Enable (CKE) pin; low-power entry is a CA command bounded by CS.
integration_overview.on_demand_wck: WCK is enabled only when a transfer is imminent (after WCK2CK sync) — a defining low-power feature.
integration_overview.no_handshake: Deterministic latency; data follows the command without per-beat acknowledgment.

interface_categories: Full-speed differential Write Clock (WCK_t / WCK_c, on-demand)
Full-speed differential Read Strobe (RDQS_t / RDQS_c, DRAM-driven on read)
Chip select (CS) — also bounds low-power-mode duration
Power (VDD1, VDD2H, VDD2L, VDDQ=0.5 V, VSS, VSSQ)
interconnect_topologies_supported: Single controller + single LPDDR5 die (point-to-point, soldered on the SoC board / PoP).
Single controller + multi-die LPDDR5 package (multiple dies, per-channel CS / clocks).
Two-channel x16 organization (two independent channels per package).
Package-on-Package (PoP) stacking over the mobile application processor.
default_signal_values_when_omitted: RESET_n must be deliberately driven HIGH by the controller before normal operation. WCK remains disabled until a transfer is imminent. Low-power mode is entered only by an explicit CA command and persists until CS next goes high.
soc_dependent_items: LPDDR5 controller / scheduler IP (Synopsys / Cadence / SoC-vendor memory controller).
LPDDR5 PHY: quarter-speed CK PLL + on-demand WCK generation, WCK2CK leveling, per-bit deskew, DFE / tx-rx equalization, RX FIFO.
DQ / RDQS read training and WCK write training engines (per frequency set point).
Link-ECC encoder/decoder (read + write) and DBI logic.
DVFS / frequency-set-point manager (FSP-OP / FSP-WR), DVFSC selecting VDD2H/VDD2L.
Refresh scheduler (REFab / REFpb round-robin; optional RFM / adaptive refresh management).
Power-management for VDD1 / VDD2H / VDD2L / VDDQ regulators (VDDQ at 0.5 V).
Vref(ca) / Vref(dq) generation per frequency set point.

pull_up_resistors_terminators.termination: On-die termination (ODT) selectable per mode register; LPDDR5 relies on ODT + equalization rather than external termination.
External precision reference resistor to ground for impedance calibration.

low_power_modes.Power_Down: Entered via a CA command (PD bit), no CKE; lasts until CS next goes high.
low_power_modes.Self_Refresh: Entered via SRE; DRAM generates internal refresh; CK may be stopped per the defined window.
low_power_modes.Deep_Sleep_Mode: Lowest standby power; entered via SRE with the Deep Sleep Enable (DSE) bit; full re-initialization required on exit.
low_power_modes.DVFS_DVFSC: Dynamic voltage/frequency scaling with VDD2H/VDD2L core-voltage selection per frequency set point.
low_power_modes.Write_X_Data_Copy: Write-X (all-zero / all-one) and Data-Copy commands reduce data-transfer activity to save power.

compatibility_notes: LPDDR5 is NOT pin- or protocol-compatible with DDR3/DDR4/DDR5; it follows the LPDDR generational line (LPDDR2/3/4/4X → LPDDR5/5X) and JESD209-x numbering.

Versus LPDDR4: LPDDR5 adds WCK/RDQS on-demand clocking, widens the CA bus to 7 bits at DDR, moves the CAS command before the read/write to synchronize WCK, increases banks to 16 (4 bank groups), reduces VDDQ to 0.5 V, and adds link ECC, DVFS, deep sleep, Data-Copy/Write-X.

Versus DDR3: LPDDR5 has WCK (DDR3 has no separate write clock), uses JESD209-5 (not JESD79-3), is a low-voltage mobile standard, and uses CA-bus command encoding (not separate RAS/CAS/WE pins). This is the key sibling-disambiguation signature.
LPDDR5X (JESD209-5B/5X) is a speed/SI extension of LPDDR5 (up to 8533 Mbps) with tx/rx equalization and Adaptive Refresh Management; it is protocol-compatible with LPDDR5 at the lower speed grades.
